title: Associativity and pushout description of Yoneda Ext composition
statement: For $\mathcal O_X$-modules on a ringed space $X$, with Ext as in [def-sc-ext-sheaf], Yoneda composition of extension classes is associative. If $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\to0$ represents $\delta\in\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal C,\mathcal A)$ and $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal W$, then the Ext connecting map defined by pushing out this short exact sequence along $\varphi$ is the class $\varphi[1]\circ\delta\in\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(\mathcal C,\mathcal W)$; consequently $(\varphi[1]\circ\delta)\circ s=\varphi[1]\circ(\delta\circ s)$ for every $s:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal C$.

source.place: Homology Section Tag 010I (extensions, Baer pushout) and Derived Section Tag 06XP (bilinear associative composition of Ext groups)

proof.text: Represent each Ext class by a composable extension (or by the corresponding derived-category morphism). The Yoneda splice of three extensions is independent of whether the first two or the last two are spliced first, giving $(g\circ f)\circ e=g\circ(f\circ e)$.

source.place: Derived Section Tag 06XP, associative composition of Ext groups

proof.text: The pushout of the short exact sequence along $\varphi$ is the coefficient-change image of its extension class. Thus the pushed-out sequence represents $\varphi[1]\circ\delta$.

source.place: Homology Section Tag 010I, pushout of extensions

proof.text: Applying the associativity identity to $e=s$, $f=\delta$, and $g=\varphi[1]$ gives $(\varphi[1]\circ\delta)\circ s=\varphi[1]\circ(\delta\circ s)$.

source.place: Derived Section Tag 06XP, associativity specialized to degrees 0 and 1
